utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours to everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT -- 04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. May we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon, Mr. Harmon, and Ms. Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Today appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic, Milos Androvic, Tina Drolec, Daniela Tasic, Gregor Guy-Smith, and Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to warn you that you are still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of your testimony, to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now remind both you and myself to make a pause after my questions and I will, after your answers, so that we do not overlap in our questions and answers, okay?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On Thursday, on the 7th, we wrapped up with the analysis of some parts of the rules of service in the security organs of the armed forces of the SFRY, and I would like to just take a look at two other articles that have to do with what you testified to during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 6063, page, in B/C/S, 12, and of the English version, page 14, and I'm interested in Article 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read out slowly this Article and I will stress certain portions of it and ask you to comment on them. Article 31 reads: "When there is information or reasonable grounds to suspect that a member of the armed forces or a member of an organisation for NVO is involved in intelligence-related or other hostile activity, or that such much activity can be justifiably expected, and if the security organ believes that, for the purposes of shedding light on this activity, one of the levels of operative processing should be introduced for this person and that other methods and means that security organs apply in carrying out tasks within their competent should be applied, or that other measures, in accordance with the provisions of these rule, should be taken through a superior security organ, they request permission to take these measures from the officer under item 17 of these rules." Now, does this Article deal with the operative work and operative measures that the Honourable Judge Moloto mentioned, using a simpler, term, spying - and you used the word processing - so is this Article related to measures that are taken such a member of a unit, if this is an threat that he could pose to the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then the request would be forwarded to an officer mentioned in Article 17, and on Thursday, when we analysed this Article, we saw that this was an individual who was authorised by the then secretariat and we concluded that this person would be either the chief of the Security Administration of the General Staff, or of the army commanders.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In reply to Mr. Saxon's question, you talked about the main tasks of the security organs. Is one of the tasks of this organ to also monitor of possible threats to a unit from within the unit itself or activities of, let's call the subversive elements within the unit, itself.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these are the measures that are mentioned in this Article; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were the security organ in the JNA and the VJ, if you obtained information that certain operative measures should be taken against any individuals, or member of a unit, you would then request authority or approval from your superior officers, and once you received that approval, you would take action; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let's see what the situation was with the methods and means applied when you were the security organ in the Serbian army of Krajina. When these members of the army came through the 40th Centre to the Serbian army of Krajina, I believe that for a certain number of them, you received information that they were already under certain measures, surveillance measures in the army -- from the former Army of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not get approval from any institution or individual of the VJ at that time to monitor that person, but you actually did that, pursuant to this rule; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then, based on this rule that you applied as a security organ in the Serbian army of Krajina, you then proceeded to do the operative processing, and then you would inform thereof the Security Administration; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you did that, because, as you explained, you used and applied the means and methods provided for in this Article; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now a general question, again, related to this area to this field. Are aware when you worked in the Yugoslav army as the security organ if an officer was sent to a mission abroad and was -- and that person who under these certain measures, surveillance measures, would that person still be under surveillance while abroad?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any specific information about any such instances, but I think such a person would not be appointed to a mission abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not speculate. But if you receive information that a certain individual is already -- an individual who is already there if you receive information that such an individual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- should be submitted or subjected to such operative measures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think this question calls for speculation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Please do not speculate just tell me, if you know in your experience of any such cases, if not, I withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I withdraw my question, Your Honour. And I will -- I have another question regarding another Article from this document. That's Article 57, subparagraph (2).

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This should be on page -- all right. We have it on the screens now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a chapter, entire chapter that deals with the Security Administration and all I would like to take a look at is Article 57, paragraph 2, which reads: "The Security Administration provides specialist management for security organs and JNA commands, units, and institutions according to the provisions of these rules and organises and directs their work of importance for security." Is that right? Now, while you were in the security organ in the Serbian army of Krajina did the Security Administration of the Yugoslav army ever direct or manage your work?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I propose -- in view of this being a very long document, and I am aware of your guidelines, but I propose that we tender into evidence just the paragraph that I showed this witness on Thursday, and the ones that I showed the witness today. I don't know what the Prosecutor's position is but this document was on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has a number of questions to ask about this document. Perhaps it might be best to wait after we see redirect examination, and then we may seek to tender the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, I would propose even now that we tender it now in its entirety, but then let's wait for completion of the redirect and then we can see whether we should tender the entire document or just the articles and their relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, how many pages is the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just coming to that. This document in B/C/S, is 52 pages long, or, rather, 96 rules or articles. Personally I believe and let me say at the outset, Your Honour, I believe that both Mr. Saxon and I will agree that we could tender certain chapters that are relevant and that are of interest for this trial and for the Trial Chamber; and in that sense, I think maybe we can reach a joint position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will admitted the pages that you have referred to now, if Mr. Saxon has to add further pages we'll add those pages at that time. So the pages that are given to [indiscernible] are admitted into evidence, may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, those pages will be Exhibit D89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if the interpreters have any problems with my microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, the interpreters do not have a problem with your -- with Defence counsel's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They have no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I whether try to keep -- to switch off my mic after my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, I have a few more questions about your relationship with the Security Administration while you were in the Serbian army of Krajina. But that, I would like to clarify a few matters that have to do generally with the status of Serbian officers in the Serbian Republic of Krajina. Would you agree with me that the Serbian army of Krajina was a unified army with all the elements in a structure that are typical of an independent army?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was established and it functioned on the basis of a special law on the army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you're probably aware that this law was passed, based on the constitution of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Members of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina had their task to defend the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, which was clearly defined.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That army had a clear chain of command which was defined in the law; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That chain of command was based on the basic principles, on which any army functions: The subordination, unity of command, and joint -- and singleness of command. Do you agree with what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And any violation of this principle of subordination and unified command would actually affect the chain of command in any army, and that would also apply to the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've provided some testimony in the Martic case on the chain of command, in the SVK, if you recall, when you answered questions about the relationship between Martic and Celeketic, especially in relation to the actual role that Martic had under the constitution. You said then and this is page 3914 of the transcript in the Martic case, that Martic was a de facto and de jure supreme commander of the SVK. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was also a Supreme Defence Council of the RSK as the supreme organ for the command and control of the SVK; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it comprised the president of the republic, Martic, at a certain time, then the commander of the SVK, the minister of Defence and the prime minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And only Martic, as president of the republic, could issue orders to Celeketic, his highest army commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the SVK was in charge of the operational work but the president of the republic approved and issued decisions on the use of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Serbian army of Krajina was a totally independent army, both in its structure an organisation, independent from the Army of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just wondering. Perhaps some foundation could be laid. What is the basis of the witness's knowledge for such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm quite sure. Is that an objection.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... to give an opinion, Your Honour, and I'm simply not sure what the basis for his ability to give that opinion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do we determine that this is an opinion that he is giving? Is he giving -- are you giving an opinion, sir, or are you giving an answer from your knowledge? I don't know. Let me defer to you Mr. Lukic. There's an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can rephrase my question. But this line of questioning actually arises from the questions that were put to this same witness in the Martic case and also the questions that the Prosecutor put to the -- the witness in his examination-in-chief. And I can also give you references of those. But I can also rephrase the question, as Mr. Saxon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you want to rephrase the question, do so by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, you performed significant and responsible duties in the SVK and you were the deputy commander of security and member of the Main Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All the questions that I have put to you, are they based on your opinion or your experience in view of the positions that you held?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you testified on Thursday, on page 5881 [as interpreted], line 19 of the transcript, you were -- you discussed -- or you talked about your transfer from the Yugoslav army to the SVK, and you said then that you were assigned for temporary duty in the SVK and that you were released of your duty in the Army of Yugoslavia and that your deputies were appointed to your post. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And on that -- at that moment practically or factually your duty -- your role in the chain of command in the Yugoslav army ended; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Through the 40th Personnel Centre, certain status-related issues and entitlements of yours were resolved, which you had previously enjoyed in the VJ, and this is something that you've already testified about; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you crossed over to the chain of command of the Serbian army of Krajina, the Chief of Staff Loncar was your superior -- or no. Initially, you held the position of assistant chief of security for operational -- or, rather, let me leave it to you to explain what it was you were.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the head of the information an analysis section, and I was subordinated to the chief of security of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both in terms of the command line and the security line.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us clear this up. Where a certain officer, as a security organ, was a member of his own security structure, that person was subordinated to the superior along the security chain of command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it Smiljanovic at the time.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially it was Vuk Dmitrovic and then it was Dusan Smiljanovic afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were pointed assistant commander for security of the Serbian army of Krajina or let's just put it simply, security organ of the SVK. In the chain of command the only person who was superior to you was General Celeketic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under the specialist chain of command, you were the highest-ranking officer of that particular chain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us briefly look at a portion of the statement you gave to the OTP, 1D00-9162.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that on our screen, please. Paragraph 82, which is at page 26 of the B/C/S version and page 18 of the English version. I'm interested in only one issue -- or, rather, one short portion of the statement. Wait for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here you referred to a report, and I'm interested in the bottom part of the paragraph, which starts with the following words: "It was inconceivable." The statement reads: "It was inconceivable that Celeketic issued such an order without the prior approval of Milan Martic. I sent my report to Celeketic and my counterpart in the VJ, Dimitrijevic, but I'm not aware of any reaction from their side." Do you still maintain the extent of what you said and that was that Aleksandar Dimitrijevic as chief of security in the VJ was your counterpart, you being in the SVK.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this must have been an error in the interpretation or I must have been misunderstood. I did send a report, but I could not describe the relationship in terms of him being a counterpart. He was a commander of the corps. Or maybe I misunderstood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you a moment ago about the fact that the SVK was an independent army, quite a separate entity from the VJ. You held the highest security position in the SVK. Aleksandar Dimitrijevic, at the time, held the highest position in the security organ of the VJ. There was a relationship of cooperation and that -- between the two of you and that's how I perceived you described your relationship by referring to him as a counterpart of yours. In other words, there was not a superior/subordinate relationship, in terms of -- of where the two of you stood.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need the document anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we remove the document. At page 13, line 19 to 20, Witness, you said -- talking about Mr. Dimitrijevic, that he was a commander of the corps. Were you being -- did you -- were you misinterpreted here or do you still say he was a commander of the corps, now that you have clarified that he was head of security, not commander of the corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This had to do with a report that was send to General Dimitrijevic, and the report had to do with Colonel Gacic, who was a corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, sorry. I'm talking about how you have been interpreted in the transcript today. I don't know whether you can see and whether you do understand the English here. At page 13 of the transcript, in front of you, at line 20, you say "he was a commander of the corps." You have just agreed now with Mr. Lukic that in fact he was your counterpart, being head of the security in the VJ. I'm just saying, which is which between those two? Were you being -- were you misinterpreted or -- or did you make a mistake when you said he was a commander of the corps? That's all I want to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my report had to do with Colonel Gacic, commander of the 39th Corps. The report had to do with husband activity. And it was about him that I reported to General Dimitrijevic. I reported to him about the conduct of the commander of the 39th Corps, Colonel Gacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear your answer, sir, but you're not answering my question. What I want to know is, was Mr. Dimitrijevic, was he your counterpart at this time; or was he commander of the corps of the VJ? Because you have given these two answers today. I just want to know which is correct and which is not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Dimitrijevic was, at the time, chief of the Security Administration of the General Staff of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He was commander of the corps. Thank you so much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see an error in the interpretation of what you asked, Your Honour. I understood you to say that he was not a commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what I said, and, yeah, it is misprinted here. It says it quotes me as saying he was a commander of the corps, but he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about the reports you sent, when you were in the JNA, VJ, and at a later date, in the SVK. When you were the security organ of the 3rd Army of the VJ, and in general, in the VJ, how often did you send reports to your superior within the security chain of command?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the SVK, you were from November 1993 up until August of 1995, for almost two years, and it was my understanding that you sent two types of reports to the Security Administration; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm getting lost because of the question you put. You're saying at line 3, page 16: "When you were the security organ of the 3rd Army of the VJ, and in general in the VJ," -- you were talking when he was in the army of the VJ. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A group of these reports were reports about the use of methods and means of operative processing, employed vis-a-vis the officers that you monitored; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The second group of these reports were pieces of information about certain events that you deemed necessary to inform General Dimitrijevic of, and there were five or six such reports spanning the entire period that you referred to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to the first group of reports, you said that there were relatively few individuals who were subjects of operative processing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At page 5922 of the transcript, line 20, and at pages 5923, 5924 and 5, you testified that Dimitrijevic did not seek reports from you relating to the security situation, rather, you sent these reports based on your personal assessment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Likewise, in relation to reports on operative processing, you sent those reports gratuitously and they were not solicited from him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that I sent these reports by way of a relationship of cooperation between two friendly armies.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the closest to explaining it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about your transfer to the SVK. In your testimony on Thursday, you described an episode which preceded your departure for the SVK, and which had to do with your superior officer, Kuzmanovic, and about the fact that he himself being -- hailing from the area of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, he should have served as an example by going there first?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding that you didn't mind the fact that did he not particularly go, rather, the fact that he seemed to be so pro activity about the entire issue without himself joining the other army.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that under the law of the Army of Yugoslavia any secondment of a soldier to another army had to be executed with the individual involved being entitled to appeal the decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not appeal the decision, pursuant to which you were sent to the SVK, did you?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at another document you were shown in your direct examination and which has to do with this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1865, can we please have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we have that on the screen, what do you want to do with 1D00-9162.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will revert to my old practice, where I will only read for the transcript a portion of a witness statement without asking for it to be tendered. This is a part of the statement that a witness gave to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document you've already testified to will now appear on our screens. You've already had an opportunity to see the document and to testify about it. This document dated 7th October 1994, which is roughly a year following your departure for the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading the preamble now: "Pursuant to the order of the VJ chief of the General Staff, strictly confidential number 3480 I, dated 4 October 1994, and after the interviews held with professional officers and non-commissioned officers with the VJ chief of the General Staff regarding transfer an appointment to the 40th Personnel Centre ..." The text follows from there. Are you aware of such interviews having been held, although, at the time you were, of course, in the SVK, that the officers that were supposed to join the SVK spoke with officers and the chief of the VJ General Staff about that transfer?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the text under item 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The text under 8 reads, and this part of the text refers to the eight individuals mentioned above: "For the above mentioned persons (I stress out)" -- "so for the above mentioned persons again (I stress again) take written statements and submit them by courier to the 3rd Army command at the latest on the 12th of October 1994." Did you know that certain officers when asked to join the SVK, had to give written statement, signing them stating that it was their wish to go or not to go and join the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just one last comment and let's see if you're aware of that? Under 21, under this number, it says Roman II mention is made that action should be taken for cancellation of service for these two individuals under number 1 and 2, termination of their professional military service. It says below that: "On the meeting held with the chief of the general staff of the VJ, the above mentioned persons stated that they would like to terminate their professional military service with their right for retirement. The above mentioned persons have to be called for an official interview immediately and their request for termination of professional military service should be forwarded to ..." and it says to whom. Are you aware of the fact that some officers because they did not wish to join the SVK or for some other personal reasons submitted their own requests for release from service. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the case of a colleague Svilar, who refused for personal reasons or family reasons to be transferred to the SVK, and he was transferred to a different post. Did he retire soon thereafter, do you know or did he remain in position?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in that new position for a very brief time, and in view of the fact that he had already met one of the requirements for early retirement he decided to retire and return to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in fact he submitted, on his own, a request to be retired; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When he decided not to go to the SVK, he was not proclaimed to be a deserter and he remained within the VJ and then submitted his request for retirement; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your group, from the 3rd Army, if I remember what you said, you mentioned that some 20 officers were transferred; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: That some 20 officers left.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there in the SVK at the time there were already quite a number of officers who had stayed behind who were in the JNA earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know maybe -- although I think you didn't know the answer to that question. Do you know overall how many officers and non-commissioned officers were there in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot provide that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also know that the Yugoslav army was established after the promulgation of the new constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under that constitution and the Law on The army, it protected -- this army protected a different territory, not the same territory that was protected -- had been protected by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was a new army, which had a different task, a different territory to protect, as it were?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more clarification I'd like to see if you were aware of it. Mr. Saxon asked you about the ethnic composition of the members of the SVK and their ethnic background and you said Mr. Celeketic was from Vojvodina. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that his family actually hails from Lika?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very well aware of that. His father, Petar, was from Lika.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Lika was, at the time, in the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And a brief question regarding your Thursday testimony, when you talked about the visits of Mr. Mrksic and General Velickovic. That's on page 5907 of the transcript and when Velickovic addressed you and said this was all the same sky, meaning the sky over Yugoslavia and the sky over the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, during Operation Flash and Operation Storm, because this was the same sky, did you receive any assistance from the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on to a different topic now and I will ask questions about certain disciplinary measures that were taken and disciplinary action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Could we now please pull up on the screens the rule on the Serbian army of Krajina. The last session, Your Honour, we only tendered one article, and now I would like to take a look at another one. That's 65 ter 06367 and I would like Article 161. Unfortunately, it hasn't been translated into English but as this is only one Article, I will read it out here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, as you can see this is part of the Law on Army of the Serbian Krajina which was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and I would just like to take at -- a look at Chapter 13 where disciplinary responsibility and action is discussed and Article 161 reads and you tell me if I have read this correctly. "As a breach of military discipline, any act of a military person" -- "any act of a military person will be considered a breach of military discipline in keeping with the rules of service and other" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Defence counsel please make sure that the proper article is on the screen for the interpreter's sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there's a request from the interpreters that you make sure that the proper article is on the screen. I see Article 161 on my screen. I don't know whether the interpreters do or not see it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do see it now. Thank you, Your Honour. But it was being scrolled while the text was being read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we not scroll it down while it is it being read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, yes, I probably just read out first the entire title of this chapter, but for the interpreter's benefit I will now read just this article, Article 161. And we haven't had this translated, unfortunately. "Any military person who takes action which is contrary to the duties of military service as provided for in the Law, shall be considered to be in breach of military discipline," so any actions that in contravention of the law, the rules of service and other provisions, orders and other enactments of superior officers which have to do with the service and especially." And then a whole number of different items mentioned, but I will only read number 2: "Absence without leave from a unit or institution or from service." I assume that you were aware of this regulation, Mr. Raseta; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those individuals who left the Army of the Serbian Krajina without leave and returned to the units of the Yugoslav army were not subject to disciplinary procedure in the Army of Yugoslavia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It hasn't been established that the witness is aware of any such individuals, Your Honour, that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta let's just talk about what the -- the things that you know. Now, do you know whether, in the Army of Yugoslavia, any proceedings would be instituted for a deserter from a member of the army of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether individuals who left without leave - a unit - were subjected to military proceedings in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All individuals who left or who were absent without leave from the SVK were subjected to proceedings and a request was forwarded to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia for such individuals to be returned to the SVK. I don't know of any instances nor I do recall that any such individual was returned to the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, just to be clear, I was asking you about the proceedings within the SVK itself. But you are talking about the requests submitted to the Yugoslav army for those individuals to be returned back to the SVK; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would there be previously disciplinary proceedings undertaken so that -- against such individuals and then, following that, there would be a request to the Army of Yugoslavia to return those individuals; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see document P1147, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes. Well, I propose, like last time for only this page or this Article, rather, to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't have it in English, sir. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I also propose then that we tender it as a MFI document, and then we will request for this entirely Article 116 to be translated into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That last point was my concern, and it has been clarified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That it be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 06367 is admitted into evidence and marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D90, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, I don't know if you had occasion to see this document already. If not, you can take a look at it, please?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the document that is before me on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just scroll it down a little bit so that the witness can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it, and this is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I will only have two questions for you. So this is a document from the Main Staff of the SVK sent, on the 14th of December, to RC RMO of the Yugoslav. Do you recall what this means?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia [Realtime transcript read in error "Yugoslav army"] I think that is what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive your salaries via this accounting centre, and the salaries were actually deposited in your accounts in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know of instances where individuals would be absent without leave and that they would still be receiving pay for that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such information, but there probably were such instances; otherwise this document would not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Colonel, Colonel Krnjajic, do you know this person. He was involved in personnel; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Now you have helped me read out the name because it wasn't very clear this is was Dusan Krnjajic, and he was the personnel officer in the Main Staff of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document into evidence. Oh no, I apologise, it is already an exhibit. I would just like to clarify something because I think there is an error here on page 27, line 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence but you didn't say of the Yugoslav army because those are different institutions?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This letter was sent, to be more precise, to the accounting service of the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When an officer from the SVK submitted a request to return to the Yugoslav army, he would have to submit that request to his superior officer in the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And on page 5927 you said that requests submitted by officers, whose tour of duty or term of duty had expired, that their request to return were discussed at the collegium of the Main Staff of the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if the collegium of the Main Staff or the officer in charge did not provide such an approval and that person left, that would actually be desertion that would be absence without leave; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you began your duty in the SVK, your post, your formation post, was established by your superior officer or the competent officer in the Serbian army of Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that information, as to what position you were posted to, was sent by their personnel service to the 40th Personnel Centre, in order to take care of the status-related issues; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During that one year, when you went to work in that army, other army, you said that Celeketic had talked to Dimitrijevic, who had told him that they did not find an adequate substitute for you, and that, therefore, you had to remain performing your duty there.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you not have any objections to make on that decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And later on, when you held the position on which you were able to speak to Mr. Dimitrijevic on a par, you did not tell him that you objected against his statement that he should -- you should carry on your duty in the army.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because he told me that he would find an adequate substitute for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the mean time, you continued with duties in the SVK and gradually were promoted to a position that was higher to any of the positions that you held in the VJ.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And your establishment post was higher than the post that you left in the VJ when you went to join the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us discuss now another document you talked about on Thursday, and that's P2333, which is Celeketic's letter, sent to General Perisic, in relation to certain SVK officers. Certain information is provided about the whereabouts of all of individuals listed in this letter; is that right? Or rather not the whereabouts but which positions and establishment posts they held.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among others under number 3, the commander of the 39 Corps is mentioned. Then also the 21st Corps is mentioned, the 18th Corps, the is 15th Corps, and finally the 7th corps. Tell us, all the corps mentioned here were, in fact, various titles for the SVK Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Corps bearing such titles did not exist in the Yugoslav army, VJ, did they?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under number 1 there is an individual mentioned who you referred to, but let us look first at the date. This is it a document dated 10 December 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under 1, the individual by the Dusan Loncar, son of Mitar is mentioned, and he is the Chief of Staff -- he is a Deputy Commander as well, and he is an OMJ colonel?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not that he occupies the position of the chief of the Main Staff of the SVK; rather, he is being nominated to that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. This nomination to the post of the Chief of Staff, his rank, which should be verified in the VJ, is that something that matters to him a great deal on account of his salary?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know how this witness can speak -- well, the answer has been given but I don't know how this witness can be ... [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether you spoke; when you spoke, your mic was on or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The witness has given his answer, Your Honour. I withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness testified to this position of theirs which later on reflected itself on their status-related rights, and I think this is something that he talked about on the direct. I may be mistaken, but I will withdraw the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is withdrawn, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To be fair to Mr. Lukic he is absolutely right, and I am withdrawing my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is withdrawn, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I suggest that we take our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Raseta, we will stay with this document for another moment. The document reads in respect of Dusan Loncar, "duty" -- let me be precise: "Duty, Chief of Staff, and, at the same time, Deputy Commander, at the Main Staff of the VJ 40th Personnel Centre." In view of your recent answer, I put it to you, and we will have a look at another document, I don't know if you will agree with me or disagree with me, at the point when this document was composed on the 10th December, he already held the position of the Chief of Staff, but this position of his had only to be acknowledged by the VJ. Would you agree with me and could you confirm for me whether he was already the Chief of Staff at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I am not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll look at another document, but let's just keep in mind the date of this document, namely, the 10th of December, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now call up document D87. Have a look at the document and I will have a couple of questions for you.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision, issued by the President of the Republic of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Mr. Milan Martic, concerning exceptional promotion of Mr. Loncar, and it's the same Dusan Loncar we referred to earlier; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you see, the date of the document is only six days after the earlier document; namely, the date is the 16th of December.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And by virtue of this decision he is promoted to the rank of the major-general. And will you agree with me that at the time he was already chief of the SVK -- or, rather, Chief of Staff, on the position of the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Simply a request. If counsel and the witness could slowdown just a little bit and perhaps pause between question and answer, because at times -- Mr. Lukic is already on his next question, but I even hear the English translation and does not give me an ability, if I can or need to, to respond or make an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. But, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The fact that -- the fact that this document is dated the 16th of December, 1994, a date after the 10th of December, it doesn't say anything about whether or not he was already Chief of Staff on the 10th of December. If it predated the 10th of December, I would understand. But I'm not quite sure whether it is serving your purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness was unable to answer either my earlier question or this one, I will not insist on this. I hoped, perhaps that the document would refresh his memory, but, evidently the witness is not familiar with the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another brief question, in relation to your Thursday testimony. I think it was at page 5930 of the transcript that you talked about the fact that Martic gave you a task concerning an amount of fuel that was supposed to arrive from Yugoslavia. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You received this task directly from Milan Martic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time when he gave you this task, he was already the president of the republic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know if the fuel was purchased in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, perhaps it had been refined in the -- at the refinery in Pancevo. You don't know by which means they obtained the fuel.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only know where it was that I waited for the column to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you did not receive the task from Celeketic but directly from the president; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now briefly discuss your reports, i.e., the reports sent to the Security Administration, and which you testified about. Let's look at document 2334?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a P document, or do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your report dated the 2nd of May, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that the gist of this report, why it was sent, was the emergency situation in which the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina found itself in the aftermath of Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you look at the first part of the document, in many respects, it seems to me to be a combat report, because it refers to the situation in the theatre of war, more of a combat report than an intelligence report, and you will correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 3 of the B/C/S version, and 5 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's one sentence that I find interesting, and I'd like to have your comment on it. You referred here to a meeting which was held by the Supreme Defence Council in its extended, enlarged form; and you say there, all the participants in the discussions and in their proposals agreed not to cave in to the Ustashas. However, there are different approaches on how to resolve the situation. Except for Martic, Celeketic and the narrow corps of the Main Staff, all the other ones were in favour of a peaceful solution to the newly arisen situation and that as a precondition they suggest that the 18th Corps commander sign a cease-fire agreement with the commander of the opposing side which would mean, which would imply, a surrender and a capitulation of this part of the territory." Mr. Raseta, you were probably familiar at the time with the fact that the leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was in favour of a peaceful solution of any sort of conflict in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have to have an audible answer from you. In your view, this piece of information which shows what line of thinking of the strict political and military leadership of the RSK was important to be conveyed to the federal leadership [as interpreted], in order to clearly see what their attitude towards the conflict was, right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, what you were doing as a security organ --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I believe that question calls for speculation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me put the question this way. Or, rather, Your Honour, what I'm seeking from the witness is a comment, in other words let me put this question to the witness. Why did you believe that you needed to convey this part of your report about the attitude that various individuals had toward the conflict? Why did you feel it important to be sent to the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The problem with -- the problem with that question is that because of the previous question, the witness has effectively been given an answer, so I don't know what weight could be given to a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do agree it's a question of weight this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my answer: A lot of time has passed in the meantime. I know that President Martic and Celeketic were not in favour of a peaceful solution to the problem. They wanted to return with -- to return fire. The other participants were of the opinion as described in the document, that through negotiations and through peaceful means, a resolution to the problem should be sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, the information, when conveyed to the federal army, about what the resolution of the conflict situation would be, would that be important to them?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That's why I informed the Security Administration thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I take it up on your behalf. Mr. Lukic, that question had just been objected to a little earlier and you rephrased it in an acceptable manner, but for the fact of weight. I don't know now why you abandon the acceptable question and go back to the objectionable question. You had asked the question, sir, why did you find it important to report this difference of opinion by Martic and Celeketic to the leadership in -- in Serbia. That was the question. He can tell you what went on in his mind at that time. But now you're asking him about why you think it is -- why he should think it's important for the Serbians to get this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that this constitutes speculation. I suppose that this was a sort of information a security organ should convey, and I believe that that's how the witness sees the situation, and I don't think this calls for speculation on the part of the witness. What is specific about this witness, perhaps we can ask him to leave the courtroom and then we can discuss the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is no need for him to leave the courtroom. When you say "in your view," that's how you started your question, you're seeking an opinion. But when you say, Why did you send this report? Why did you find it important to send this report; you're asking him about what happened in his mind. The way you are putting the question, you want him to tell us what happened in the mind of the people to whom he was sending the report, and that is speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you see the difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. I'm trying to rephrase the question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, at the time when you sent such reports, was it important that you do convey information to the allied [Realtime transcript read in error "applied"] army?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Because this was a very delicate situation, the situation in which some elements of the SVK found themselves, and that's why I thought it important to inform my chief of the administration about it. The chief of the specialist department of my corps was killed. This is something that is not mentioned in here and that's why it was very important for me to convey the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that would have been important, because the corps -- the chief that particular section was sent through the 40th Personnel Centre; is that why?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But he had held the rank of lieutenant-colonel; that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, the information was information -- was important -- at the time you compiled this report, you felt that it was important for the information to be perceived as important for the security of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're waiting for me. I have nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Oh, yes, right. I didn't see it in the transcript. Sorry. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at another report and that is P1018. This is another interim report, one of the group of reports which dealt with the situation; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was sent on the 3rd of August of 1995, at the time of the commencement of Operation Storm, in the territory of the RSK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 2, please, of the B/C/S version, and page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph two acronyms are mentioned. And can you tell us what they stand for, HIS and SOS of -- of the Western countries. Do you see that in the second paragraph. HIS or SOS of the western countries?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: SOS is the foreign intelligence services, and HIS, that's short for Croatian intelligence service. I can't give you the exact title. S stands for security in Croatian. At any rate, it is the Croatian intelligence service and foreign intelligence services of the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph you say: "It was ascertained that over 80 percent of the disinformation was sent through UNPROFOR. In most cases through liaison officers and various friendly relations, but in both cases making sure that the disinformation reaches the highest levels (commanders of brigades)," et cetera. Could you explain or interpret this. What is this about? What type of disinformation are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember the specifics right now. I know that there was -- there were such instances and I know that we verified that, but I cannot recall at this point what they were about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, according to you, was it important at this time, in terms of security of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, to know how the UNPROFOR functioned in view of the negotiations that were under way where the Yugoslav role was significant?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They to be significant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove this document. And could we now please pull up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do so, sir. I have been to trying desperately to find the acronym, SOS, on the English version of this document and I'm not seeing it. Can I see it on the B/C/S version. Maybe I'm missing something somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolute right, Your Honour. In English it says western security and intelligence services and that's probably the full name of the -- actually the development of the acronym. And that's the same problem that we've had before with the translation service, where the acronym is missing, and I agree with you there is no mention -- there is no acronym SOS appearing in the English translation. SOS means foreign intelligence services, and it was correctly translated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up Exhibit P2336.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have already testified in relation to this document. This is a report prepared by you that was sent on the 26th of May, 1995, but it was sent to the commander of the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And my understanding, as to the contents of this document, is that you -- that it is to be checked why the order that was issued by General Celeketic, the order to shell the Sisak refinery, why it was not carried out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at the date of this document. It's dated 26th of May, 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In fact, you're sending this report to the new commander of the SVK, who was appointed on the 18th of May, 1995, General Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just bear with me a moment. I will have a few questions about the dismissal of -- or replacement of General Celeketic and we should try and remember this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, in any case, as claimed in the indictment, General Mrksic was appointed as the commander of the SVK on the 18th of May, 1995. If you don't recall the date, I won't insist on it.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the exact date. But it was in May, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I have to note, as you read the entire report, to me, it seemed illogical that this was sent to General Celeketic where in fact you are discussing General Celeketic in the report itself.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information that you related to the commander of the SVK on 26th of May, that Gacic did not carry out the orders, you did not submit this report to the Security Administration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now just a few questions regarding the daily situation reports that were sent by the command of the Main Staff of the SVK to, among others, the General Staff of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the president of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, could we please pull up document 1023 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: P or 5? The interpreter is not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does P or 5 mean, sir? This document 1023 is it an exhibit already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. Exhibit P1023.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the order by General Mile Novakovic when he was a commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Krajina. You've already testified to this. You said that he assumed but you weren't sure that VSO meant the Supreme Defence Council of the federal republic and it says: "In order to achieve full and high quality drawing up of combat reports and their timely submission to the VJ GS ..." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you list a number of bits of information that -- and reports that are to be drawn up, such as the movement of enemy forces and so on. You are aware and you're familiar with this type of information; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up another document, Exhibit P1617.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you have already seen this document, so I will give you a chance to see it now and read it. If you've read through this document let me ask you this: This document is dated 6 February, 1993. Before you left, you were transferred to the SVK, now, do you agree when you read this document and see what the purpose of this request, as it is stated here, and when you compare it to the previous document, that, in fact, the purpose or the goal, the end is the same. The request refers to the same goal.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since I did not take part in the drafting, and I wasn't there at the time I could not really give you an answer. Have I my opinion about it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no. Let's not go there. But would you agree with me in terms of what type of information is requested here, it is similar to the one that we've seen earlier sent by General Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in essence, it's about the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And mention is also made in this document, this request, that these reports be submitted that they should also be sent to the SVK. Now let me ask you: Did you -- was there in place a system of exchange of information with the VRS, both in terms of security and operative information?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say almost none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what you said in your report. But do you know whether intelligence and combat operation -- information was exchanged in such reports?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, are you aware of the systems of communications that existed in the former JNA, that existed on the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia, that it was not broken up, that it remained in place?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very little about that. I don't know exactly what it is that you would like me to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, simply do you know of instances of any army, including VRS, SVK, JNA, the Croatian Army, the HVO, the BiH Army, that they could actually use that same system, communications systems that it remained from the previous, the former Yugoslavia that they were in a position to use it, if they were trained properly?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up document P2335.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've testified to this document in the examination-in-chief. Can I ask you this: What is the meaning of these numbers that are added, that are handwritten. We see the 15th, 11th, 21st, 39th, 18th K.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that this same report was submitted to the commanders of the 15th, 11th, 21st, 39th and 18th Corps of the Serbian army of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 3 in the B/C/S version, and 4 in English, the portion referring to the security situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph it says: "UNPROFOR members and members of other international organisations continue to perform intelligence work against the RSK.
