In this period, the following activities of these organisations have been registered." And then it goes on. Now the same question that I asked before. At the time when these reports were drafted and some members of your organ, as you said, participated in the drafting, did you consider that sending this information regarding the UNPROFOR was important?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like to ask you a few questions about your testimony regarding the shelling of Zagreb in May 1995. You testified in detail in the Martic case regarding this matter. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also provided some information in this respect in your statement to the OTP, and I assume that you had occasion to see this statement during the prepping for this appearance in court?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D00-9162, pages 21 in B/C/S and 15 in English. Paragraph 70 of your statement to the OTP, your 2005 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said it is 1D00-9162.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. 1D00-9162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I will read this because I see that it carries on, onto the next page but I'm reading the first sentence in B/C/S: "Based on my information as head of the security organs of the SVK, Martic and Celeketic were the only ones who knew about the location of the Orkan MBRL and who was in charge of" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic -- Mr. Saxon, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very sorry to interrupt. It's just that in the original English version of the statement the sentence that Mr. Lukic just read is quite different if I'm reading the correct sentence. In the English version it says: "Based on my information as head of the security organs of the SVK," and I'm wrong because I'm reading the wrong line. I apologise for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hmm. Perhaps I should read it in English that would be best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just very sorry, it's simply so the record is clear. It's just that Mr. Lukic referred to the first sentence and is he referring to the first sentence at paragraph 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be as precise as possible, I will read the relevant part in English, since the English version is the official version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that paragraph of your statement you say: [In English] "Based on my information as a head of security organs of the SVK Martic and Celeketic were the only ones to know about the location of the Orkan MBRL and who was in charge of protecting them. Martic and Celeketic were also the only ones who could decide about the use of Orkan ..." [Interpretation] This is what the statement says and you do stand by the statement today, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 73 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pull it up, please. I'm interested in the third sentence. Can we turn to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here you state: [In English] "As I said earlier in my understanding that -- it is my understanding that the only Martic Celeketic were involved in the decision making protest to shell Zagreb with Orkan?" [Interpretation] You still stand by that statement today, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will not seek to have the relevant portions admitted, since we have them in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pull up document P496, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose you're familiar with the document?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the classic combat order issued by the commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date is the 1st of May, 1995 when it was sent to whose command exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 7th, 21st Corps and Battalion of the military police of the Main Staff of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And nobody else?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, you did not see a single document report or piece of information where Celeketic or Martic informed anyone in the Yugoslav army, in the VJ, about this order.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now turn to the answers you gave in relation to your retirement. In your testimony on Thursday, page 5946, you said that you went back to the VJ upon a prior approval from General Mrksic. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, General Mrksic was your superior officer in the Serbian army of Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You went back to the VJ, or, rather, into the territory of the FRY without his approval based on what we read from the provisions of the Law on Army, in other words, you wilfully left the ranks of the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you joined the Yugoslav army, or rejoined the Yugoslav Army, there was no post available corresponding to your position or rank, and that's why you applied for retirement.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You submitted your application to the relevant unit that was your home unit before you left the army for the SVK.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I still have several questions for you on a different subject. You attended the collegium of the Main Staff of the SVK when Celeketic showed you his written resignation, that he intended to submit and he held the position at the time of -- of the commander.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you personally saw the document and the -- and Celeketic explained to you what it was about.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall General Celeketic telling you or anyone else earlier on that he would resign if any part of the territory of the RSK came to be occupied or ended up in the hands of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said at the collegium of the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And following Operation Flash, a certain portion of the RSK was no longer in the hands of the Serbian army of Krajina; in other words, it was occupied, captured, or re-taken, depending on the side viewing the situation.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm interested in 65 ter document 6103.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you're familiar with the document. Have a look at that time, and I'll have a couple of questions. The document is self-explanatory. The date is 18th of May, 1995. I asked you earlier when it was that Commander Mrksic was appointed, but you weren't sure of the date. Did you know that, at the time, the Assembly of the RSK carried a decision to release General Celeketic from the duty of the commander of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see the document. I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, have you heard of Rajko Lezaic and did you know that he was the president of the Assembly at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I have this document admitted, Your Honour. Is it one of the documents from the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D91.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move into private session for a couple of my questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. May you close your cross-examination in open session, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, any re-examination, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may have but a moment to set up the podium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before Mr. Saxon starts, I have to make two corrections of the transcript. Page 38, line 1, and page 36, line 19, I used the term allied army, army of allies and I think something else was recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 38, line?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 38, line 1, and page 36, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My page 38 doesn't refer to any allied thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can assist, Your Honour, I have that term on page 39, lines 13 to 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that at line 14. You say in line 14 should read allied and not applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 36, line 19, federal leadership. [Interpretation] I said allied and not federal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a correction that you want to put. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: About a document that my colleague also showed you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This would be 65 ter 6063.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's now D89. If you can refer to it by its exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm told only seven pages were tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We'll see if, perhaps administratively, at the end of this examination, what would be the best way to deal with this document. If we can turn, please, to Article 21 at this time, which will be on page 10 in the English version and page 9 in the B/C/S version. If we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can take a look at Article 20, Colonel -- excuse me, Article 21.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which refers to: "An active duty serviceman who was sent according to service requirements to work in another state organ, organisation of associated labour or other organisation."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, I would like to move from this article, if I may, please, to Article 30, on page 14 and page 12 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see in the -- I believe my colleague showed this article to you during his cross-examination. And this article talks about sending reports to the following parties concerning data gathered and the results of checks conducted. And the second paragraph refers to: "Other officers of commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces, concerning other data that is important for the security and combat readiness of these commands, units, institutions and staffs." Was it pursuant to this article that you continued to monitor persons, officers from the VJ, certain officers from the VJ, who had been sent for -- for service in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite a different matter. This has to do with the verification of certain information from the field of security, information sent to the organs competent to take charge of security issues. That's number one. Number two, if the situation dictates that some other senior officers be informed of certain information, then the information will be conveyed to such officers as have the competence to act upon the information. So this is quite separate from the other matter that you put to me about the surveillance conducted in respect of certain individuals who were members of the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, then, would this paragraph give you an obligation, for example, while you were serving in the SVK, to provide information, for example, to the Security Administration of the VJ General Staff.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If methods and means normally employed the security organ are, indeed, applied. So the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 18 in the English and page 15 in the B/C/S version. This is in chapter IV, which is entitled the powers and obligations of officers in security organs in performing their duties. And if you could turn your mind -- actually, I may have erred because I want to look at Article 43 which may be on the next page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If could you direct your attention to Article 43 for a moment, Colonel Raseta.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: While you were serving in the SVK, between 1993 and 1995, did this Article give you the authority to arrest a person and deliver him to a military court or a military institution of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did discuss the document with the witness, but I did not touch upon this subject. I think that Mr. Saxon has gone beyond the scope of my cross-examination. Had he wanted to examine the witness on these issues, he could have used the document from his list. In none of my questions did I touch upon criminal prosecution in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, that may be, Your Honour, except what Mr. Lukic did touch upon and the whole tenor of his use of this document were the witness's powers and authority pursuant to this document, particularly while he was serving in the SVK, and it seems to me I should be able to explore that with this document on re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite briefly, I think that this is a very broad interpretation of my cross-examination. I touched upon very specific and clear topics arising from the document. This does not in any way touch upon my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, for one thing, he discussed officers who deserted, Your Honour. That was one topic of his cross-examination. And, for example, such a topic might fall within the purview of this article in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be a topic -- would that be conduct that would be justiciable within a military court or would that be a disciplinary inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to testify; it seems that would be a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would conduct, for example, such as desertion in the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina, would such conduct be referred to a military court, or would it be referred to some kind of a disciplinary inquiry, or both?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. This paragraph, quite unambiguously, places the obligation about the security organs to proceed as regulated in this article. However, the military judiciary in the SVK was non-existent. In other words, we were unable to apply these provisions. Had it been possible we would have dealt with the problems of desertion, incitement to mutiny and other conduct which constitutes a threat to security upon the request of the prosecutors' offices and the military courts of the FRY did not have jurisdiction over the SVK, or, rather, the RSK territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Raseta, quite independently of this document here, the question simply is: Would desertion constitute a crime justiciable, in the military courts, or would it be a matter for disciplinary inquiry? Can you just answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This does not fall within my competence. It falls within the competence of the courts. I think it does fall under criminal prosecution; the desertion, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what you think. That is not fact. The correct answer is it doesn't fall under your competence, so you don't know. Then, of course, you added an opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I must rule you out of order -- I must have sustained the objection by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to what is Article 48, which is on page 19 of the English version and page 16 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could review, Colonel Celeketic [sic], please, Article 48?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Review, Colonel Celeketic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, I should have said Colonel Raseta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Have you seen Article 48?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Article 48 -- on cross-examination my colleague asked you about the position you held in the VJ, before you went to the SVK and the fact that you were promoted while you were serving in the SVK. This particular article describes the obligations of an authorised officer of the security organ to carry out tasks within the competence of the security organ assigned to him. Regardless of whether or not these tasks are covered by the work that is regularly conducted in their establishment position. My question for you is: While you were serving in the SVK -- let's maybe -- step by step. When you first went to the SVK in October 1993, what establishment position did you hold in the 40th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Saxon please speak into his microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My duties were twofold. My first duty was that of a chief of the information analysis department of the security department of the SVK Main Staff, and the second duty was of the chief of the security Department of the SVK Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were these duties reflected as your establishment positions in the 40th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. Would this be the appropriate time to take the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] indeed, it is. We will take a break and come back at a quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Colonel Raseta, during his cross-examination, my colleague, Mr. Lukic, at page 16, lines 12 to 15, asked you whether the Security Administration of the VJ General Staff ever directed or managed your work while you served in the SVK, and your answer was no. I'm wondering whether you could take a look at Article 95 of these rules of service, which would be on page 31 in the English version, page 26 in the B/C/S version, the chapter entitled: Work of security organs in exceptional circumstances in imminent threat of war and in war. I see Article 95 moves over onto the next page. If you could read the first part of it, Colonel, and then perhaps we could go to the next page in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The same with the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This article: "Authorises the chief of the Security Administration to prescribe specialist instructions on, inter alia, the work of security organs in gathering information on security checks and on individuals, and on the work of security organs, on their preparations for work in war, an imminent threat of war and other exceptional circumstances." My question for you is: During the time that you served in the SVK, did you receive any - to use the term here - specialist instructions from the chief of the Security Administration of the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, other than the individuals that were under operative processing, in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, who were later transferred to the army of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does that mean you received some instructions about these individuals from the chief of the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall what those instructions were?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were to monitor their activities during their stay in the -- or service in the army of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, just so the record is clear, did these individuals come from the Army of Yugoslavia to the army of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender the articles that I have shown to the witness, at this time, from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those articles are admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The pages tendered by the Prosecution now will be added to the exhibit that constitutes the pages that were tendered by the Defence, and they will come under one exhibit number. And I think that was Exhibit D89.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Colonel, just to follow up on my last question, these instructions that you received from the chief of the Security Administration to -- to monitor the activities of these individuals during their service in the SVK, were you obliged to follow these instructions?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was certainly obliged to follow these instructions, because their activities that they were already engaged in, in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia were assessed to -- the possibility was foreseen that they might continue to engage in the same kind of activity in the army of the Serbian Krajina, which would then threaten the army, and this is the reason why we had to monitor them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say that "the possibility was foreseen that they might continue to engage in the same kind of activity in the army of Serbian Krajina, which would then threaten the army," in that response when you used the phrase, "the army, which would threaten the army," which army are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian army of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So needed to report to the chief of security of the -- of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia regarding these individuals who might do something that would threaten the army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this was not the wording that the witness used, and I think this -- there was an error in interpretation, or, rather, the Prosecutor phrased or framed this question in a different manner, and I would request that he use the proper wording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is the proper wording?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wouldn't want to give any of my comments because that may be perceived as leading question. But I think that the Prosecutor should not actually draw his own conclusions as to what the witness had said, but, rather, pose a question. And if he wishes to refer to what the witness actually said and draw conclusions therefrom, then he should point out the exact words of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, do you have any response to that objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Quite frankly, no -- no, Your Honour. In my mind, it is a proper question. The witness can answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's just look at the question as you had put it. Actually, that question seems to be a repetition of what the witness had just answered to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I will withdraw it, Your Honour, and I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But just let me make sure that -- you asked him previously from page 64, line 25 and when you say that "the possibility was foreseen that they might continue to engage in the same kind of activity in the army of Serbian Krajina, which would then threaten the army." In that response, when you used the phrase "the army," "which would threaten the army," which army are you referring to? And he said: "The Serbian army of Krajina." Then you asked the same question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, in my mind, Your Honour, it was not the same question because I was simply trying to clarify exactly with a was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. What is the difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour. I -- I cannot enunciate a clear difference, so I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We can now leave this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Colonel Raseta, during his cross-examination today - and this is at page 10, lines 1 to 3 - you agreed with my colleague's question that the SVK was totally independent of the VJ. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like perhaps to explore this area with you a little bit. Was the SVK dependant on VJ officers to make up the Main Staff of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A leading question, Your Honour, suggests an answer that should be given. This is a question that could be answered yes or no. It is not leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you had testified earlier today that the SVK was completely independent of the VJ, and so I want to explore that. Maybe I can step back for a moment. While you were serving in the SVK Main Staff, where were you and the other members of the SVK Main Staff assigned to, vis-a-vis the VJ, if anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand your question either. What do you mean by "vis-a-vis the VJ"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: While you were in the SVK Main Staff, did you and your -- were you and your colleagues member of the 40th Personnel Centre of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were members of the Main Staff of the Serbian army of Krajina. And as for the 40th Personnel Centre, that was the centre via which we were transferred to and later on returned to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show -- I want to actually --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: First of all, I will ask you about some names. While you were in the -- serving in the SVK, did you know a man named Stojo Spanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon already put this question during his examination-in-chief, and the witness answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, but in a different context. During --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you mean -- is that a context in which you wouldn't know him? If he did know him in any context at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, Your Honour, I was not clear. I simply wanted to explore with the witness the numbers of officers who were sent from the 40th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, ask about the number of personnel. Don't ask about the person that he already answered to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know how many -- while you were serving in the SVK Main Staff, whether the corps commanders of the SVK were attached to the 40th Personnel Centre of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "attached"? I don't understand. Do you know mean subordinated or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were they temporarily assigned to the SVK through the 40th Personnel Centre, if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is P -- Exhibit P875, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can take a look at this document, Colonel Raseta. You see it's from the 14th of May, 1994, from the Main Staff of the SVK to the Yugoslav army General Staff. And it says: "In order to replenish RSK aviation units, we require the following officers ..." And then there is an long list. Was the SVK dependant on the Army of Yugoslavia to man its aviation units?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as personnel is concerned, I have already explained on several occasions, that they were actually manned -- the units were manned by officers from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, including pilots and everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were these officers sent under orders of the -- sent to serve in the SVK under orders of the Army of Yugoslavia, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see this list, and I don't know whether this request was actually granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Colonel Raseta, it is completely my fault. My question wasn't clear. You had mentioned earlier, a moment ago, that the SVK units were manned by officers from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, so I was referring to those officers that were sent to serve -- well, that served in the SVK. Were those officers ordered or sent to the SVK under orders by the VJ, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. You had testified previously, including today, about how after a year -- your first year of service in the SVK, you requested permission to return to the VJ. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And eventually that request was denied by General Dimitrijevic, first, and then that was passed -- that message was passed down --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I withdraw -- I anticipate the objection and I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you do anticipate one, rephrase immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That request was denied; is that right, eventually?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not quite like that. General Dimitrijevic said that he did not have suitable replacement for me, so he did not really deny my request, but once the possibility opened, he would actually look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, and I stand corrected. And that's because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you object to him standing corrected?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It's rather the interpretation of this portion of the testimony, page 70, line 24, the witness did not say he would actually look at it. He worded it different, that it would be; he didn't say who. But here, it appears that, as if Dimitrijevic was the one who said that; whereas, that is not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question to the witness, please, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question simply was -- and all we need is a yes or no answer, the request -- your request to return to the VJ after one year was denied. That's right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now I'm a little bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your request -- I thought that when you requested to return to the VJ after one year eventually that request was denied. Am I wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not wrong about it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just want the record to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you had specialist skills for which General Dimitrijevic did not have a replacement at that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, not Vasiljevic; it was Dimitrijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I said Dimitrijevic but perhaps you heard Vasiljevic. And those specialist skills, your specialist skills, were also needed in the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not that I was not replaceable or that I was so indispensable but there was not an adequate replacement for me, and the commander said that I should stay until I was replaced. I don't know if I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that replacement was supposed to come from the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So was the SVK Main Staff, then, at least with respect to your post, chief of the security department, was it dependant on the VJ to fill that post?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the question calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well the witness was serving there at the time. He was -- he was -- he is and was intimately aware and involved of the situation. Perhaps we can ask him if can he answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to answer the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question addressed to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. That is ... Do you know at all whether the SVK Main Staff depended on the VJ to filled post that you were occupying in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. The post should have been occupied by an experienced officer who had performed all the duties I had performed who had adequate schooling. That sort of personnel was not available in the army of the -- of the Republic of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What about fuel? Was the SVK dependant on the VJ for receiving adequate fuel supplies, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered that question in the affirmative. The priority was to look for fuel and lubricants and to seek these from the General Staff of VJ. As far as the command and control was concerned, the SVK Main Staff was independent of the General Staff of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can a modern army operate in war without sufficient fuel?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, it cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where did the SVK get its laws and rules of service from? Did it draft all of them by itself?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which laws and rules of service you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, all right. For example, the rules of service that you've seen here today and on Thursday, the rules of service of security organs in the armed forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Were those rules of service then used in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can accept the question as it stands now. It was the earlier question that was formulated differently which I had a problem with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I don't think you did -- yes, you should answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules and instructions of the administration -- of the Security Administration of the FRY were used by the security organs of the SVK. We did not have our own instructions in the SVK. All the instructions we used were the instructions of the Security Administration of the General Staff of the army of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you aware whether the RSK Law of Defence adopted provisions of the Law of Defence of the FRY or the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is too technical a question for the witness. I think Mr. Saxon should first ask the witness whether he is familiar with the laws, whether he knows when the laws were adopted and only then should he proceed to ask the witness to infer any sort of a conclusion. The question as put now I think is too demanding of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, my colleague discussed the RSK Law of Defence with the witness during his cross-examination, so it would appear to me that the Defence at least believes that the witness is competent to deal with this law. But I can rephrase my question, if Your Honour so desires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, how do you know what is in the mind of the witness? Or how do you come to the conclusion that the question is too technical for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I proceeded in the following way. I first showed the witness the laws and then asked him certain matters related to the command and control and to the fundamental principles underlying the army. Those were my questions. Now, Mr. Saxon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is how do you know that the question is too technical for the witness? Why can't the witness tell us if the question is too technical for him and say, I can't answer that question because it is too technical. How do you know the mind of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept your guidance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may put your question, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know, Colonel, whether the RSK Law of Defence adopted provisions from the Law of the Armed Forces of the SFRY or the Law of Defence of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The questions I put to the witness had to do with the Law of Governing the Army alone and not one of my questions had to do with the Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question then to address the Law of the Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do so, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was under the misperception that it was the RSK Law of Defense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know, Colonel, whether the law of the SVK, or the Law of the Army of the RSK adopted provisions from the Law of the Armed Forces of the SFRY or the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia? No, excuse me, I will rephrase my question. Do you know whether the Law of the SVK or the Law of the Army of the RSK adopted provisions from the Law of the Armed Forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We can move this exhibit now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were the SVK officers who were assigned to the 40th Personnel Centre dependant on the Army of Yugoslavia for their salaries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't put a single question about salaries. Can Mr. Saxon please reference the relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Mr. Saxon's argument was and still is that you asked the witness whether the SVK was completely independent of the VJ, and he is trying to show dependance of the SVK on the VJ. He is not talking about salaries per se. He is talking about dependance, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I don't have the transcript in front of me, if I remember correctly my question was whether the SVK, under its organisation and structure, was a fully independent army. I think that I was very specific in the questions I put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I also don't have the transcript before me. I do not remember you talking about structure and organisation, but I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I proceed then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If -- if I'm not sure whether we are able to ascertain -- to find out where -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... page 8, lines 4 through 6, if Mr. Saxon can give us some other reference, if he has one. That was my question I gave you the reference for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have a different reference, Your Honour, and I think the next reference which I was depending on and which I referred to earlier puts a slightly different gloss on the issue. At page 10 beginning at line 3, question was: "The Serbian army of Krajina was a totally independent army, both in its structure and organisation, and then independent from the Army of Yugoslavia; correct?" Answer was: "Correct."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Page 10, Your Honour, starting at line 3. And it's that last part of the sentence that I am exploring and have I been exploring with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then Mr. Lukic is right. He was talking about structure and organisation. Whatever structure an organisation mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, structure an organisation can refer to personnel; it can refer to salaries and benefits; it can refer to laws which govern how an army was structured and organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you will have noticed my earlier questions and the line where they were heading. I was concentrating on the principles underlying an army and that was the question as I formulated it for this witness. I was interested in the fundamental principles of an army. You will remember that the entire line of questioning had to do with precisely those fundamental principles of the army. The question that was referenced here was also very specific. I believe that Mr. Saxon is touching upon topics that go well beyond the scope of my cross-examination. I took your guidance on board, but what is being referred to here was not the subject of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Lukic had wanted to limit his question, he could have stopped his question this way: "The Serbian army was Krajina -- the Serbian army of Krajina was a totally independent army both in its structure and organisation." He did not do that. He then continued, "independent from the Army of Yugoslavia." Which is the critical point of that question, Your Honour, which I should be allowed to explore and clarify on redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon, then the objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Colonel Raseta, going back to my question, which was were the officers that were serving in the SVK who were assigned to the 40th Personnel Centre of the VJ, were they dependant on the Army of Yugoslavia for their salaries?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, in fact, such officers received extra pay for serving in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were the SVK officers who were assigned to the 40th Personnel Centre of the Army of Yugoslavia dependant on the Army of Yugoslavia for their retirement benefits?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I'll tell you, I have a little problem with your re-examination. It's re-hashing the examination-in-chief. That's my only problem. We've heard -- all these questions we have heard before, they depended on the VJ for personnel, salaries, for fuel. That's my only problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will leave this topic now, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 17 of today's transcript, lines 14 to 16, you described the relationship between you and General Dimitrijevic of the Security Administration of the VJ General Staff, as a relationship of cooperation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But there were at least certain areas where -- certain areas of your work where you actually had a duty to communicate with General Dimitrijevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can have the Court's indulgence for a moment please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, for example, these areas included communications related to persons from the VJ, who were serving in the SVK, who might be subject to operative processing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number one, the witness already answered the question; and, number two, this is leading again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During cross-examination today, your testimony was that the individuals who were absent without leave from the SVK were subjected to proceedings and a request was sent to the General Staff of the VJ for such individuals to be returned to the SVK. Do you know -- are you aware of instances where this occurred?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean am I aware of instances of individuals wilfully leaving the ranks of the SVK and moving on to the FRY? Do you know -- are you referring to that category of officers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that here, at page 25, line 18, you can find the witness's answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You talked briefly during cross-examination about what happened after your first year in the SVK and your request to return to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Why did you request to return to the VJ after that first year?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that is what the order stated; that's to say, the order seconding me to the SVK for a period of up to a year. Since the one-year period was about to expire, I intended to submit an application for my return to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. During his cross-examination, you and my colleague, Mr. Lukic, discussed the fact that eventually you -- when you were in the SVK, while you were serving in the SVK, you were promoted to a higher post within the SVK than the post that you had left in the VJ. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question, then, is - if you know - after you received this promotion, while you were serving in the SVK to a higher post, was your personnel file in the 40th Personnel Centre amended to reflect that fact?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, to use the terms of some of our documents, in your file in the 40th Personnel Centre, did you receive a higher establishment post?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a higher level duty and a higher post, yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And commensurate with that, did you begin to receive a higher salary while you were still serving in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I have the Court's indulgence for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness Exhibit P2336. And can we scroll down in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll recall, I believe you mentioned on cross-examination that you had tried to check, as you put it, why the order to shell the Sisak refinery was not carried out. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, indeed, it was your belief that the -- that Colonel Gacic had not carried out the order of General Celeketic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, document ID 0639-8938. If we can just take a look at the first page, please, that the head line and underneath the head line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a newspaper called "Vjesnik, Croatian Political Daily." Dated Zagreb, Tuesday, 2nd of May, 1995. Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps we could zoom in on the B/C/S on the date, please. It's very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you see that now?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in more on the date, please. A bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read it now?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read "Zagreb," but I cannot figure out the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about if I give you a hard copy of this article. Would that help you perhaps, if it's a better copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could the usher please assist me, please. This is a hard copy of the same page. Can we show it to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ma'am, can you show it to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have two problems with this document, Your Honours. This document was not on the 65 ter list, as my associates inform me; and, on the other hand, I really can't see -- of course, Mr. Saxon hasn't asked the question yet. But I don't see and I would call him -- call upon him to tell us which portion of my cross-examination he is linking up to. I don't see how this document is in any way linked to my cross-examination. And this is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me take the second point first. This -- during cross-examination, my colleague showed the witness both a paragraph from his statement, which -- and asked him questions related to the fact whether this particular order to shell Sisak was carried out; and he also showed the witness an exhibit which we have just seen, 2336, and the witness talked about part of the purpose of his work in getting this order was to find out why the order to shell Sisak -- shell the Sisak refinery was not carried out. So, if I can, this document deals with the events at Sisak, Your Honour, which -- and I would like to explore that with the witness. It's true this was not op our 65 ter list, but I could not anticipate the line of cross-examination, yeah, from my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem with this because I still think that my portion -- I still have a problem with this position of Mr. Saxon's because it is my claim that the topic that I touched upon in cross-examination, referring to Sisak and not the shelling of Sisak itself, and Mr. Saxon had opportunity in his examination-in-chief to ask questions about this. Now, if you recall my questions had to do with the chain of command and who received what information. My cross-examination, with regard to his report to General Mrksic of the 26th of May had exclusively to do with whom the report was sent to and whether it had been sent to someone from the Army of Yugoslavia. And if Mr. Saxon wants to touch upon those topics by using this document that can then arise from my cross-examination, but, otherwise, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to clarify a topic that the witness raised in response to questions posed by counsel during his cross-examination, and I can't think of a more basic purpose of redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the trouble is we don't know what topic you want to clarify, number one. Number two, I'm sitting here and wondering if that topic arose out of a discussion of an order within an army how that gets clarified by a newspaper. This is my -- I'm just wondering -- I mean, what does the newspaper got to do with what is happening inside the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The newspaper has to do with whether a particular event occurred or not, Your Honour, which is directly related to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But your colleague says he never concerned himself with whether or not an event occurred. All he concerned himself with was to whom that report was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But the witness concerned himself with that point, whether the event occurred or not. That is my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, there you are, Mr. Lukic. He says the witness did refer to an event that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Or did not occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or did not occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me a moment, Your Honours. The only thing that I can find, Your Honour, about this document was on page 42, line 10, where the witness discusses and says that he doesn't know the date of -- of this event. And I think that Mr. Saxon is now here seeking to obtain answers to the questions that he failed to pose during his examination-in-chief. This is not something that was included in any of the answers of the witness that now need to be clarified. Re-examination -- the purpose of re-examination is to clarify issues that arise from cross-examination and the questions that the Prosecutor asked had nothing to do with the cross-examination, and the Prosecutor is now seeking to re-examine this witness in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, actually, Your Honour, I misspoke a moment ago because I said that this topic arose from a response from the witness. That was incorrect. The topic arose from a question of my colleague. If you take a look at page 42, lines 14 to 17. "Q. And my understanding as to the contents of this document is that you, that it is to be checked why the order that was issued by General Celeketic, the order to shell the Sisak refinery, why it was not carried out; is that right? "A. Yes." I want to explore that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, I understand that. And as I say, are you not able to explore that using that order or using his knowledge? Are we now going to -- I'm not quite sure how this newspaper comes into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next page of this newspaper addresses the matter that was raised in this question, and that is what I want to explore with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And why is that matter not raised in the documents of the army? Why do we now go out of the documents of the army to find out what happened in the army from a newspaper? Any way we don't know the question. Just go ahead and everybody will be listening to what you are going to be asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Can the usher please show the witness the hard copy of the document to see if he can read the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read the date now?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please, in both languages. And it's very difficult to read. Can -- there is an paragraph in the third column. Can we focus or zoom in on the third column, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to read -- I cannot read that first word. It looks like "nirim." Are you able to read that paragraph or where that bullet point is there, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to. It's really illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in any more on that bullet point on that column?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the word "Sisak" there?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The town of Sisak."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to read about what it says about the town of Sisak?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is really illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about now?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The town of Sisak is ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: "Or was."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the rest is completely illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I see the time. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one or two questions for the witness. I hope it won't be too long. I too -- make it short. If I understood you correctly, when you were asked to go to the SVK, you didn't do it on a voluntary basis; it was not your idea to go.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you forced to go or did you just obey your orders?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply obeyed the order that I was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have another question for you. Do you know what is the percentage of officer of the Serb army that went to the -- to the SVK. So the VJ officer what is the percentage of VJ officers who is went to the SVK?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any knowledge of that percentage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I would like to know is not the percentage of the officers of the VJ who went to the SVK, but I would like to know what is the percentage of the VJ officers serving in the SVK, with respect to the amount of officers in general. In other words, amongst the SVK officers there were 50 percent of officers compared to the VJ, 60 percent, more or less?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a bit difficult to give you an answer to that. But mainly what I can say is that most key positions were occupied by officers from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and I mean command posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have another question for you, and I hope that we can be brief. You said that there was a good cooperation between your services within the RSK and the VJ, right, which explains the reports. This is why you were sending your reports to the VJ. Was it also the same the other way around? Would you receive regularly VJ reports?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was not really -- it did not really go both ways. It was not really good cooperation.

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean orders, I did not receive such documents. But if you mean exchange of information, I did receive that. So I did not receive orders, but from time to time, we exchanged information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But what I wanted to know is, did you receive or would you receive reports from the VJ on the military situation, for instance, in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were sending reports, and did you also get reports from the Serb Republic of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question. Very seldom; almost not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well. That's all. Thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to have any questions arising, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Raseta, the Honourable Judge Picard asked you about exchange of information. When you contacted Mr. Dimitrijevic did you receive from him some information as to what the positions of the political leadership of Yugoslavia was -- were, with reference to what their positions and their opinions were in connection with the situation in Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe there were some mention of them but not officially. Maybe we did exchange information just unofficially, but -- but through reports, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean in your being counterparts and when you had direct communications, did he sometimes relay information that was relevant to you of intelligence interests?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, sometimes that would happen, but it was not -- they were not orders. They were really exchanges of operative information in the sense of exchange of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the sense of cooperation?

utterances.speaker: RADE RASETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just apologise to everybody for having gone beyond the time. Just trying to get done with the witness. Thank you, sir. That brings us to the end of your testimony. You are now excused. You may stand down and please travel well back home, and thank you so much for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Due to the lateness of the hour, the Chamber stands adjourn until tomorrow, 2.00 in the afternoon, in Courtroom I -- I'm told Courtroom II, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. Court adjourned.
